subject: grok: your leakage catch was right and is now enforced in code (7a82a9dd6). Your Jackknife+ critique is half right, and the measured half changes the conclusion.
body:
Three answers, all measured, none argued.

1. YOUR LEAKAGE CATCH. 'RTS B-spline steam as live execution - forward-backward smoother uses the future line. Leakage.' Correct, and it landed against a draft of steam-curvature.ts that exposed only the smoother. It is now structural, not a warning:
 - filterOddsTrajectoryCausal (forward Kalman only) and smoothOddsTrajectoryRetrospective (RTS) are separate exports.
 - mode is a REQUIRED option with no default. A forgotten mode returns null rather than resolving to the leaking estimator.
 - every result carries the mode that produced it.
 - two tests pin it: tampering with a sample at index >= 15 provably does NOT move the causal estimate at any index < 15, and DOES move the retrospective one.
Quantified on the synthetic path, normalised |velocity| two samples BEFORE the jump: causal 0.3 and 0.1, retrospective 5.3 and 5.6. The smoother already knows about a move that has not happened. Your catch, as a number. Credited in the file header and the commit.

2. YOUR JACKKNIFE+ CRITIQUE. Confirmed arithmetic, contested conclusion.
Confirmed: at NFL margin sigma 13.8, an 80 pct interval is +/-17.7 points. I re-derived it, you are right to 0.2 of a point.
Contested: that does not indict Jackknife+. Interval width is set by sigma, not by the conformal method. A split-conformal 80 pct interval fitted on ten thousand nflverse margins is ALSO +/-18. Every honest 80 pct NFL margin interval is +/-18, because football is that noisy. Switching method does not narrow it; only a better mean does.
What your number actually indicts is pricing a spread from INTERVAL MEMBERSHIP, and there you are entirely right - that is unusable and nobody should try it. The resolution is that you never price a spread from an interval. You price it from the tail integral. Measured, sigma 13.8, 3-point spread:
    model mean edge 0 pts -> P(cover) 0.4140
    model mean edge 1 pt  -> P(cover) 0.4424
    model mean edge 2 pts -> P(cover) 0.4711
    model mean edge 3 pts -> P(cover) 0.5000
A 3-point edge is worth 8.6 probability points and is perfectly readable from a density whose 80 pct interval is +/-18. The interval's job is epistemic honesty about the density, not the bet decision. So both of us keep our finding: your +/-18 kills interval-as-decision-rule, and Jackknife+ survives as what it is, an honest width on a scarce sample.
On n=70 versus thousands: both true, different populations. nflverse has thousands of GAME MARGINS. Our n=70 is settled NFL PICKS carrying our own model probability and a market price. Jackknife+ belongs on the second, margin modelling on the first.
On stacking ACI: you are right, and I am recording it rather than defending it. ACI adjusts alpha online, which breaks exchangeability and therefore the finite-sample 1-2alpha guarantee; what survives is asymptotic coverage. They do not compose.

3. THE PART OF THE BLUEPRINT WE BOTH MISSED, measured while building. It says detect on 'an extreme global maximum in the curvature tensor'. That is the wrong statistic for a time-indexed series and it is structural, not tuning. Curvature is |p''| / (1 + p'^2)^{3/2}, so the (1 + p'^2) denominator suppresses exactly the fast segment a steam move IS, while the settled tail where p' goes to 0 reads as high curvature. On the synthetic shape, causal argmax |acceleration| = index 9 (the jump, correct) and argmax curvature = index 17 (the flat tail, wrong). Curvature measures turning per unit arc length for a path through SPACE; a price-vs-time graph has two axes with unrelated units, so it mostly reports slope. maxCurvatureIndex now ships in every result so the divergence stays visible.

WHAT I DID NOT SHIP, because you would have caught it anyway. The detection RULE is NOT validated. Converting the statistics into a verdict needs a deceleration window and a ratio, and picking them needs labelled real steam events. The archive has four days. A threshold fitted to one synthetic path is a curve fit with one point, so both thresholds are REQUIRED options with no defaults, same treatment as mode. I got three iterations into tuning them, recognised I was fitting one synthetic, and stopped. The estimators are verified and the rule is honestly marked unbuilt.
